solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Corrupt assistant married retiring go-between

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the string built from the first three words is read backwards

parts.note: to rot is to corrupt or decay
an aide is an assistant
M is the abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: A crooked aide, now wed, steps down from brokering deals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corrupt' looks like an adjective on the assistant, but it is a verb giving its own piece; the whole run is then reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A go-between carries messages and settles disputes between two parties, which is exactly the role of a mediator.

clue.text: Rebuilding harms east end of city resembling Slough

indicators.note: rebuilding means putting together in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: on a map east is the right-hand side, so the east end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the last letter of city

explanation.surface: Redevelopment damages the eastern side of a town like Slough.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is a town west of London, so the clue reads as urban planning; with a lower-case s, a slough is a swamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A slough is a bog or swamp, so ground resembling one is boggy and wet.

clue.text: Easing of hostilities briefly interrupted by stray nuclear weapon?

definitions.note: the question mark flags a definition by example

indicators.note: interrupted by means something breaks into the middle of the word
briefly says the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: detente is a relaxation of tension between nations
to err is to stray from the right path

explanation.surface: A wandering warhead briefly disrupts a thaw in the Cold War.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stray' looks like an adjective on the weapon, but it is a verb meaning to go wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear arsenal is the classic example of a deterrent, a weapon meant to discourage attack.

clue.text: Duck eggs served up in diner for starters

indicators.note: in a down entry, served up means brought upwards, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: ova is Latin for eggs

indicators.note: starters are what come first, so only the opening letters are kept

parts.note: the first letters of in and diner

explanation.surface: A café menu offering duck eggs as a starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' is a bird on the menu here, but it is the verb meaning to dodge.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck something is to dodge it, a verb synonym of avoid.

clue.text: Go too far on ladder

parts.note: on top of is over
a ladder in tights or stockings is also called a run

explanation.surface: A warning not to climb too high up a ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a ladder is also a line of unravelled stitches in tights, which Americans call a run.
explanation.definitionFit: To overrun is to exceed a limit, such as a schedule or a boundary.

clue.text: Despicable individual I'm relieved to hear should be indoors now

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the time when a curfew is in force rather than a noun

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible person

indicators.note: to hear tells us the exclamation is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: the exclamation of relief, spelt as a word meaning a small number

explanation.surface: Someone sneers that they're glad a nasty type must stay at home.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic paraphrase: when it is curfew, everyone should be indoors now.
explanation.definitionFit: A curfew is an imposed hour after which people must stay inside their homes.

clue.text: Boxers possibly subject to damage over time

parts.note: under in the sense of subject to, as under orders
wear is gradual damage from use

explanation.surface: Fighters in the ring take a battering as the years go by.
explanation.walkthrough: Boxers suggests fighters, but here they are boxer shorts.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxer shorts are one type of underpants, an example of the category.

clue.text: Play around near resting place

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the first word wraps the next

parts.note: play is fun, amusement
to in the sense of close by, as in a door pulled to

explanation.surface: Children romp near where someone lies, perhaps a grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resting place' suggests a grave, but it is a mattress you sleep on.
explanation.definitionFit: A futon is a Japanese-style mattress on which one sleeps, a literal place for resting.

clue.text: Aggravated witness withholding name in brief statement

indicators.note: brief says the word is cut short by its last letter
withholding means keeping something back inside, so one word holds the next

parts.note: a word is a brief statement, as in a word of warning

indicators.note: in places that combination inside the last word

parts.note: to see is to witness
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: An irritated witness keeps a name out of their short testimony.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest here: the name goes inside the witness, and that inside the shortened statement.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggravated means made worse, as an aggravated injury, so it matches worsened.

clue.text: Limited availability of network radio's lost work unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters end up in a bad, jumbled order
lost means the following word is dropped out of the longer word before it

parts.note: taken as written before its tail is removed
the letters removed from the first word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A broadcaster's scant output is blamed on lost work across the radio network.
explanation.walkthrough: Network minus work leaves NET; joined with RADIO and mixed up it gives RATIONED. 'Availability of' just ties the definition in.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rationed is handed out only in limited, controlled amounts, as food was in wartime.

clue.text: Who blue-pencilled it originally, at least in part?

definitions.text: Who blue-pencilled it originally, at least in part?

indicators.note: in part says only a portion of the run of words is wanted, so look inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of blue-pencilled, all of it and the start of originally

explanation.surface: A question about who first struck out a passage with a blue pencil.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: blue pencil is the traditional tool for marking cuts in copy.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue-pencilling means censoring or cutting text, the classic job of the person who prepares copy for publication.

clue.text: Inclination of Republican politician charged by America

indicators.note: charged by suggests being headed or led by, so the letter for the country goes in front of the politician

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Republican
A is a common abbreviation for America
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: The leanings of a Republican lawmaker indicted by the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged by America' means headed by the letter for America, so A sits in front of MP.
explanation.definitionFit: Inclination here is a slope or incline, and a ramp is a sloping surface.

clue.text: Did career finish off employee in firm?

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the word that follows

parts.note: firm means hard; it wraps round the other piece

indicators.note: finish off points to the final letter of the next word

parts.note: the last letter of employee

explanation.surface: A question whether a staff member's job ended at the company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' looks like a noun about a working life, but it is the verb meaning to rush headlong.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to rush wildly; to have hared is likewise to have run very fast, like a hare.

clue.text: Modify plans to raise freedom of movement

parts.note: to rear is to raise, as with children
range is the scope within which one can move

explanation.surface: Changing one's arrangements to win more liberty to move about.
explanation.definitionFit: To modify plans is to arrange them again in a different way; a verb phrase matching the verb.

clue.text: Agrees to have child

parts.note: to have something, as to have a cold, is to get it
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: A couple consent to start a family.
explanation.definitionFit: People who get on are on friendly terms and agree with one another, an idiomatic phrasal verb.

clue.text: Most genuine support comes after seeing that

indicators.note: comes after tells us the following word is placed behind the next phrase

parts.note: since means seeing that, because
a rest is a support, as an armrest

explanation.surface: The truest backing arrives once you have watched something.
explanation.definitionFit: Sincere means genuine and heartfelt, so the superlative is the most genuine.

clue.text: Get ready to make cuts in advance

parts.note: pre- is the prefix meaning before or in advance
to pare is to trim or cut back

explanation.surface: Planning budget reductions ahead of time.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists the cutting before the advance, but the prefix comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To prepare is to make ready, the transitive synonym of get ready.

clue.text: Praise speech following publicity

indicators.note: following tells us the speech is placed after the publicity rather than before it

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a piece of publicity
an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A speech of acclaim given after a publicity campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' puts the speech after the publicity, so the short piece comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is worship and veneration, praise in its most devoted form.

clue.text: Find disguise belonging to detective

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector; DI's means belonging to the detective
a cover is a disguise or false identity

explanation.surface: Uncovering a detective's undercover outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists disguise first, but the possessive piece leads the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To find something out is to discover it; the verbs are close synonyms.

clue.text: Great Britain at last isn't involved with Europe's borders

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the gathered letters are mixed together
at last picks the final letter of the place name before it

parts.note: the final letter of Britain
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

indicators.note: borders are the edges, so only the outside letters of the word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of Europe

explanation.surface: A Brexit-era remark that Britain finally stays out of European affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great Britain' reads as one name, but Great is the definition and only Britain feeds the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Great in the sense of extreme in degree, as in great heat, matches intense.

clue.text: Doctor barely tastes food

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the remaining letters are reshuffled
barely suggests stripping something bare, so the word loses its outside letters

parts.note: taken as written before its outer letters go

explanation.surface: A physician hardly samples any of the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Strip the outer letters of tastes to leave ASTE, then rearrange. 'Doctor' looks like a person; here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is informal slang for food, as in a snack bar promising good eats.

clue.text: Distress curtailed difficult dispute

indicators.note: curtailed literally means having its tail cut off, so the next word loses its final letter

parts.note: hard means difficult
a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: Anguish cut short by a tough argument.
explanation.definitionFit: To harrow is to distress or torment someone, as in a harrowing experience.

clue.text: Spooner's much more out of it and confused

indicators.note: Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words, so that swap is wanted

parts.note: much more is way, more out of it is higher; swapping their opening sounds

explanation.surface: Someone far more intoxicated and muddled than before.
explanation.walkthrough: High is slang for out of it on drugs, so much more out of it is way higher.
explanation.definitionFit: Going haywire means behaving erratically or getting badly muddled.

clue.text: Reforms what PM's inauguration requires?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: mends or makes improvements

definitions.note: a cryptic phrase for the time of day changing, read as A.M. ENDS
definitions.meaning: second, cryptic meaning: the afternoon can only begin when the morning finishes

explanation.walkthrough: PM suggests a Prime Minister being sworn in, but it is post meridiem: for p.m. to start, a.m. ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Amends as a verb means alters for the better, as when a law is improved, matching reforms.

clue.text: Trade writer trapped in vehicle test

indicators.note: trapped in means held inside, so one piece sits within the others

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
to try is to test
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A craftsman's writing implement got stuck during a car's roadworthiness check.
explanation.definitionFit: Carpentry is the skilled trade of working wood, a craft one can follow for a living.

clue.text: Harry tries something to improve Mark?

indicators.note: to harry is to harass and disturb, so the letters that follow are knocked out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Harry tries to help his friend Mark do better.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry and Mark look like two people; one is an anagram signal and the other an exam grade.
explanation.definitionFit: A resit is a second sitting of a failed exam, taken to raise one's grade.

clue.text: Maintain case for commercial objective

indicators.note: a case is the outside casing, so only the outer letters of the next word are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of commercial
an aim is an objective

explanation.surface: Arguing for a business goal in a sales pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case for commercial' reads like a business argument, but case means only the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain something is to assert it as true, which is what you do when you claim it.

clue.text: Daily Mail's original attraction

parts.note: a daily is a cleaning woman who comes in each day, also called a char

indicators.note: original means the first one, so only the opening letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the first letter of Mail

explanation.surface: What first drew readers to a British tabloid newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Mail is a British newspaper, but daily alone is old British slang for a charwoman, a domestic cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: Charm is the power of pleasing or drawing people in, the quality of attraction.

clue.text: Container ship

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a receptacle such as a jug or bowl

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a container ship carrying freight; the two words are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a hollow receptacle for liquid and a seagoing craft.

clue.text: Withdrawing no one imposition provided that thing

indicators.note: withdrawing means pulling back, so the whole string that follows is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one
a tax is an imposition or levy
if means provided that

explanation.surface: Someone backing out of a burden on condition nobody else pays it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Provided that thing' looks like one phrase; provided that is the conditional, and thing alone is the definition, as in having a thing about something.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a thing about something means an obsession with it, which is a fixation.

clue.text: Take turns to judge entertaining books

indicators.note: entertaining means hosting a guest, so the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: to rate is to assess or judge
OT is the Old Testament, the books of the Hebrew scriptures

explanation.surface: Panel members alternate in assessing amusing books.
explanation.definitionFit: To rotate a duty is to have people do it in turn, the same as taking turns.

clue.text: End period of study at Harvard?

parts.note: a term is a division of the academic year
Harvard is in the US, so at Harvard is in the US

explanation.surface: The close of a semester at an American university.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that Harvard is just an example of a place in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminus is the end of a line or route, the final stop.
